title: ROTABLOCK: Looking for Android Play Testers! A new twist on a classic block puzzle game.
author: ManagerOfClankers
selftext:
Hey everyone!  
  
I’m getting ready to launch **RotaBlock**, a neon arcade puzzle game where you place falling pieces, rotate the entire board, and complete concentric rings to clear them. You not only compete against yourself, but against the global score board!

I’m looking for Android users to join the closed test and provide honest feedback before it goes live on Google Play, especially around controls, difficulty, performance, and anything confusing or broken.

If you’re interested, comment below or DM me with the Gmail address you use for Google Play. I’ll add you to the test and send the installation link.

Thanks! Any feedback would be hugely appreciated.   
  
\*This game's assets, music, sprites, and even game trailer were made using AI! Primarily leveraging OpenAI ImageGen and Codex for still marketing material, code, and sprites. I utilized Omni Flash for some of the trailer you see above after feeding it some example images/logos/gameplay video. Happy to give insight on any of the process!\*  
  
\-ManagerOfClankers, Head of [TinyPeopleProject](https://www.tinypeopleproject.com)

comments.author: Accomplished-Sea3176
comments.body:
This is not a new twist, been done before, this just looks like a less polished version of   
[https://x.com/FreyaHolmer/status/2033942518895628485](https://x.com/FreyaHolmer/status/2033942518895628485)

replies.author: ManagerOfClankers
replies.body:
Hey there, I appreciate the feedback! However, I have to disagree. The game you linked is a gravity/weight driven game using color completion logic, and not a rotational board that you control with keys and using grid/ring completion logic independent of color.   
  
I can't also really agree that one guy dropping pieces in a demo is less polished than a whole app that is GDPR compliant with a global high score database that is hosted and internationally accessible!
